# Roulette (curve)

::: {#o1 .subject cue=lead name="Roulette"}

*Image: Cycloid f.gif.* [Cycloid](wikipedia://en/41638) - curve generated by a rotating point on a wheel

*Image: EpitrochoidOn3-generation.gif.* [Epitrochoid](wikipedia://en/1547292) - Wheel rotating around a wheel

In the [differential geometry of curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_geometry_of_curves), a **roulette** is a kind of [kinematic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinematic) [curve](wikipedia://en/89246), generalizing [cycloids](wikipedia://en/41638), [epicycloids](wikipedia://en/713354), [hypocycloids](wikipedia://en/592735), [trochoids](wikipedia://en/2738094), [epitrochoids](wikipedia://en/1547292), [hypotrochoids](wikipedia://en/1547158), and [involutes](wikipedia://en/840704). On a basic level, it is the path traced by a curve while rolling on another curve without slipping.

:::

::: {#o3 .definition cue=heading name="Definition"}

## Definition {#Definition}

### Informal definition {#Informal_definition}

*Image: RouletteAnim.gif.* A green [parabola](wikipedia://en/23231) rolls along an equal blue parabola which remains fixed. The generator is the vertex of the rolling parabola and describes the roulette, shown in red. In this case the roulette is the [cissoid of Diocles](wikipedia://en/820041).[^o41]

Roughly speaking, a roulette is the curve described by a point (called the *generator* or *pole*) attached to a given curve as that curve rolls without slipping, along a second given curve that is fixed. More precisely, given a curve attached to a plane which is moving so that the curve rolls, without slipping, along a given curve attached to a fixed plane occupying the same space, then a point attached to the moving plane describes a curve in the fixed plane called a roulette.

### Special cases and related concepts {#Special_cases_and_related_concepts}

In the case where the rolling curve is a [line](wikipedia://en/946975) and the generator is a point on the line, the roulette is called an [involute](wikipedia://en/840704) of the fixed curve. If the rolling curve is a circle and the fixed curve is a line then the roulette is a [trochoid](wikipedia://en/2738094). If, in this case, the point lies on the circle then the roulette is a [cycloid](wikipedia://en/41638).

A related concept is a [glissette](wikipedia://en/53708787), the curve described by a point attached to a given curve as it slides along two (or more) given curves.

::: {#o7 .definition cue=heading name="Formal definition"}

### Formal definition {#Formal_definition}

Formally speaking, the curves must be [differentiable](wikipedia://en/330206) curves in the [Euclidean plane](wikipedia://en/15575410). The *fixed curve* is kept invariant; the *rolling curve* is subjected to a [continuous](wikipedia://en/6122) [congruence](wikipedia://en/39330) transformation such that at all times the curves are [tangent](wikipedia://en/31482) at a point of contact that moves with the same speed when taken along either curve (another way to express this constraint is that the point of contact of the two curves is the [instant centre of rotation](wikipedia://en/18947076) of the congruence transformation). The resulting roulette is formed by the [locus](wikipedia://en/542465) of the generator subjected to the same set of congruence transformations.

Modeling the original curves as curves in the [complex plane](wikipedia://en/217628), let $r,f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb{C}$ be the two [natural parameterizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_geometry_of_curves#Length_and_natural_parametrization) of the rolling ($r$) and fixed ($f$) curves, such that $r(0)=f(0)$, $r'(0) = f'(0)$, and $|r'(t)| = |f'(t)| \neq 0$ for all $t$. The roulette of generator $p\in\mathbb{C}$ as $r$ is rolled on $f$ is then given by the mapping:

$$t\mapsto f(t)+(p-r(t)) {f'(t)\over r'(t)}.$$

:::

:::

::: {#o9 .statement kind=statement/generalization cue=heading name="Generalizations"}

## Generalizations {#Generalizations}

If, instead of a single point being attached to the rolling curve, another given curve is carried along the moving plane, a family of congruent curves is produced. The envelope of this family may also be called a roulette.

Roulettes in higher spaces can certainly be imagined but one needs to align more than just the tangents.

:::

::: {#o11 .example cue=heading name="Example"}

## Example {#Example}

If the fixed curve is a [catenary](wikipedia://en/7163) and the rolling curve is a [line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29), we have:

$$f(t)=t+i(\cosh(t)-1) \qquad r(t)=\sinh(t)$$

$$f'(t)=1+i\sinh(t) \qquad r'(t)=\cosh(t).$$

The parameterization of the line is chosen so that

$$|f'(t)| = \sqrt{1^2+\sinh^2(t)} = \sqrt{\cosh^2(t)} = |r'(t)|.$$

Applying the formula above we obtain:

$$f(t)+(p-r(t)){f'(t)\over r'(t)} =t-i+{p-\sinh(t)+i(1+p\sinh(t))\over\cosh(t)} =t-i+(p+i){1+i\sinh(t)\over\cosh(t)}.$$

If *p* = −*i* the expression has a constant imaginary part (namely −*i*) and the roulette is a horizontal line. An interesting application of this is that a [square wheel](wikipedia://en/742349) could roll without bouncing on a road that is a matched series of catenary arcs.

:::

## List of roulettes {#List_of_roulettes}

::: {#o13 .table cue=table}

| Fixed curve | Rolling curve | Generating point | Roulette |
|---|---|---|---|
| *Any curve* | [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | Point on the line | [Involute](wikipedia://en/840704) of the curve |
| [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | *Any* | *Any* | [Cyclogon](wikipedia://en/48890342) |
| [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | *Any* | [Trochoid](wikipedia://en/2738094) |
| [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | Point on the circle | [Cycloid](wikipedia://en/41638) |
| [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | [Conic section](wikipedia://en/19008673) | Center of the conic | **Sturm roulette**[^o18] |
| [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | [Conic section](wikipedia://en/19008673) | [Focus](wikipedia://en/1032607) of the conic | **Delaunay roulette**[^o20] |
| [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | [Parabola](wikipedia://en/23231) | [Focus](wikipedia://en/1032607) of the parabola | [Catenary](wikipedia://en/7163)[^o22] |
| [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | [Ellipse](wikipedia://en/9277) | [Focus](wikipedia://en/1032607) of the ellipse | **Elliptic catenary**[^o22] |
| [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | [Hyperbola](wikipedia://en/14052) | [Focus](wikipedia://en/1032607) of the hyperbola | **Hyperbolic catenary**[^o22] |
| [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | [Rectangular hyperbola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectangular_hyperbola) | [Center](wikipedia://en/4850775) of the hyperbola | **Rectangular elastica**[^o26] |
| [Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_%28mathematics%29) | [Cyclocycloid](wikipedia://en/54285001) | Center | [Ellipse](wikipedia://en/9277)[^o28] |
| [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | *Any* | [Centered trochoid](wikipedia://en/18079550)[^o30] |
| Outside of a [circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | *Any* | [Epitrochoid](wikipedia://en/1547292) |
| Outside of a [circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | Point on the circle | [Epicycloid](wikipedia://en/713354) |
| Outside of a [circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) of identical [radius](wikipedia://en/1780815) | *Any* | [Limaçon](wikipedia://en/641715) |
| Outside of a [circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) of identical [radius](wikipedia://en/1780815) | Point on the circle | [Cardioid](wikipedia://en/642101) |
| Outside of a [circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) of half the [radius](wikipedia://en/1780815) | Point on the circle | [Nephroid](wikipedia://en/843192) |
| Inside of a [circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | *Any* | [Hypotrochoid](wikipedia://en/1547158) |
| Inside of a [circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | Point on the circle | [Hypocycloid](wikipedia://en/592735) |
| Inside of a [circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) of a third of the [radius](wikipedia://en/1780815) | Point on the circle | [Deltoid](wikipedia://en/769176) |
| Inside of a [circle](wikipedia://en/6220) | [Circle](wikipedia://en/6220) of a quarter of the [radius](wikipedia://en/1780815) | Point on the circle | [Astroid](wikipedia://en/769163) |
